comparator.sourceNotes: The Amsterdam VU-UT curriculum is represented by its 41 Amsterdam-specific positive-credit compulsory study units totaling 150 EC plus genuine generic minor 30 EC. Five compulsory 30-EC semester themes are context only and are not stacked with their children. Research Skills 5 EC precedes the BSc Assignment 12 EC under the current progression rules. University of Twente remains the awarding institution and VU the delivery partner.

alternatives.concept: Develop mathematical system models, algorithms, data methods and robotics alongside product design, life-cycle assessment, circular resource technology and renewable-energy analysis. progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, 180 EC, PPD in year one and ten advanced courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort semester. Programming precedes algorithms and optimisation; Mathematical Methods precedes all later mathematics, robotics and neural-network work; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes recovery, resource and renewable-system study.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete and substantively distinct related-fields curricula are feasible. The first combines mathematical systems, algorithms, robotics, product design, energy transition, life-cycle analysis and resource technology. The second retains the quantitative, robotic and product-design spine while replacing four energy/circular-technology courses with brain, neurobiology, perception/action and higher-function study for the explicit healthcare-technology direction. Neither is represented as Mechanical Engineering. A third structures/materials/manufacturing route cannot obtain statics, mechanics of materials, dynamics and vibrations, thermodynamics, fluid/heat transfer, metallurgy/polymers, tribology, precision engineering, manufacturing processes or the repeated mechanical build-test sequence from the workbook.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both establish calculus and linear-algebra foundations for quantitative system models; the external course is embedded in mechanical engineering.
UCR directly develops matrix, vector-space and linear-transformation methods; the external component combines these with further calculus.
UCR provides numerical equation and differential-equation methods relevant to finite-element computation, but not elasticity theory or finite-element mechanics.
Both develop differential-equation methods; UCR also covers multivariable and complex analysis without a mechanics application sequence.
Both analyse systems through mathematical models; UCR directly covers transfer functions, state-space and signal flow.
Both provide probability and statistics for quantitative modelling and research.
UCR studies robot kinematics, planning and manipulation, with partial control-system relevance; it does not reproduce control engineering or mechatronic hardware.
Both use a team design-and-development process involving requirements, modelling and prototyping; UCR does not reproduce structural/mechanical design or manufacturing.
Both directly evaluate environmental impacts across product or process life cycles.
Both address renewable-energy technologies; UCR emphasises technical/economic system assessment rather than mechanical energy conversion.
